answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before submitting jobs or earning reputation. Verifiers audit completed work and slash bonds when accounts are proven coordinated duplicates or fraud. A glacier of cheap identities still needs a separate stake for each account; detection across a mesa of accounts can forfeit those stakes. The attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, making a disposable plume of sybils costly rather than free.
